text: Job hunting outreach is a numbers game played badly. People blast the same template to strangers and get silence. Job Hunt Signal is an agent that finds real roles, real referral targets, and writes outreach that earns a reply. More importantly, it gets measurably better every time it runs by reading its own traces.

Paste a resume and target criteria, then run the hunt. The agent searches live job listings, finds three plausible referral targets per role from public profiles, and drafts a personalized message for each, with a hard rule against inventing profile URLs. Every draft is scored from one to five by an LLM judge on personalization, specificity, ask quality, and tone. You can edit, copy, and send a message, then log what happened. Those outcomes become the signal for the next iteration.

Everything you just saw is traced in Arize Phoenix. One run becomes a full span tree: job search, referral lookups, nine drafts, and their evaluation scores. Open a draft span and the self-improvement loop becomes visible. Before writing, the agent queries its own past traces for the highest-scoring messages on the same keywords, retrieves three proven exemplars, and uses their strongest patterns. The judge score is written back onto that same span, so observability data becomes queryable memory.

Does self-retrieval actually help? We held the resume, criteria, and judge constant. In round one, retrieval is off. In round two, the agent pulls its three best past drafts as exemplars. Average judge score climbs from four point two five to four point six four. The agent learns to imitate what already worked: a precise technical detail, the recipient's team by name, and a fifteen-minute, time-boxed ask. The same loop lifts the older Gemini two point five drafter by more than twice as much. The weaker the writer, the more its own memory helps.
Job Hunt Signal. Gemini for the agent, Phoenix for the memory. Real roles, better outreach, and a learning loop you can measure.
